item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's well written, but there just isn't enough… here. Not enough content to grab the reader. No vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think the logistics of it were clear; I was more concerned with the repetition of "walk" and "gate" (to designate two different walks, to boot). In any case, it reads much better now!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
He takes a short walk from the lab to a gate, turns right, and begins walking. In a half hour, he should return to the gate (because the path is circular).

You are right, I never had him enter the gated area. I tweaked it so now he actually goes through the gate before he starts walking on the path.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It is, after all, a story about a path (two of them, in fact).

However, that is a lot of "paths". Pared it down quite a bit.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: You've also got a first sentence that states that the MC is about to take a short walk to a gate—followed by a second sentence wherein he starts a short walk, to a gate.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, that was one of the main source of repetition, though I know that was kinda inherent to the story.

You've got a positive rating so far anyway.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I second this.

He began running through the equations in his head as he looked down the path. The curve of the new path was less pronounced than the original path, and it appeared that the new path climbed in a clockwise direction. He made some quick mental calculations, and was fairly certain that this new path would intersect the original close to the gate.

This segment, particularly, stands out quite a lot, but there's even more of them.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Is it the repetitive he/him?

My goal to was to write this without naming the character or writing in first person. That leaves me with limited ways of referring to the character.

Not really an excuse, but it's all I've got.
